target_customer: AR developers and early adopters, later enterprise and design teams buying a developer headset
problem: Computing was stuck on flat screens; Meta wanted to let people see and manipulate virtual 3D objects in the real world with their hands, replacing laptops and phones with glasses.
business_model: Hardware sales of AR headsets and developer kits (META.01 preorder 667 dollars, Meta 2 at 1,500 dollars) with an app ecosystem

founders.name: Meron Gribetz
education: Columbia University, dropped out (studied neuroscience and computer science per press)
founders.background_notes: Comcast says he dropped out of Columbia to start Meta. TechCrunch 2016 says the founders originally come from Israel.

founders.name: Ben Sand
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and co-CEO on the YC page; later at Strong Compute (W22).

founders.name: Raymond Lo
education: PhD in electrical and computer engineering, University of Toronto per YC page (listed as a Toronto university)
founders.background_notes: YC page says about 10 years of wearable and computer vision research; he later joined Intel.

exit.reason: Lost a funding round in 2018 when a Chinese lead investor backed out, faced a patent suit, and the lender foreclosed and sold assets for less than owed. The IP went to Meta View, backed by Olive Tree Ventures.

competitors.name: Google Glass
competitors.what: Heads up display glasses; TechCrunch says Glass cannot do the same AR tasks

competitors.name: Vuzix M100
competitors.what: Smart glasses with 720p display in upper right of view

competitors.name: Epson Moverio
competitors.what: Semi transparent display glasses; Epson also supplied optics for the Meta prototype

competitors.name: castAR
competitors.traction_then: Blew up on Kickstarter in October 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Building wide field of view see through optics, hand gesture tracking, depth cameras and an SDK in a head mounted device was research grade hardware and computer vision work in 2013.

defensibility.rationale: Optics, gesture interface and patents were hard to match for a small team, but large platform companies could invest far more and a patent suit later hit the company.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Glass was already shipping to developers in 2013 and big platforms later launched competing headsets. Meta itself collapsed in 2018 and 2019 and its IP was acquired from the lender.

market_need_then: Google Glass drew attention to wearable displays in 2013 and Meta's Kickstarter in May 2013 nearly doubled its 100,000 dollar goal, showing developer interest. Enterprise demand was claimed later in 2016 coverage.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch in August 2013 said the product name META.01 suggests many revisions to come; the reason for the company name itself is not stated.
branding.domain_note: Company site metavision.com; the company acquired SpaceGlasses.com for early sales, which TechCrunch called hilariously self aware (2013-08).

identity.visual_style: Futuristic headset hardware with developer focus
identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious, aiming to replace laptops and phones with AR glasses

branding.brand_signature: Meta glasses and the SpaceGlasses brand for the first product

rebrands.why: Early product was sold through SpaceGlasses.com and the Meta name was used for the company and META.01; reason not sourced.

branding.community_and_virality: A May 2013 Kickstarter nearly doubled its goal and drew coverage from MIT Technology Review, The Register and TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: A successful Kickstarter, early press and a Series B with strategic investors show real visibility among AR developers, but the generic name was later overwhelmed when a much larger company adopted it.

outcome_analysis: Meta went from a May 2013 Kickstarter and YC to a 23 million dollar Series A in 2015 and a 50 million dollar Series B in 2016, with 73 million dollars raised in total. In 2018 a Chinese lead investor withdrew from a new round, most staff were furloughed, a Genedics patent suit arrived and the lender foreclosed and sold assets for less than owed, with the IP moving to Meta View in 2019. Cash burn on research grade hardware and failure to close the next round were the core causes.
notes: The Series B valuation is derived from filings TechCrunch saw (up to 307M post money depending on share count) and is an estimate. Series A of 23M led by Horizons Ventures is confirmed by TechCrunch 2016; other Series A investors (BOE, Danhua Capital, Commodore Partners, Garry Tan, Alexis Ohanian and others) appeared only in search result summaries of press I did not open and are omitted. Total raised is 73M per Roadtovr and 2016 coverage while one outlet cited nearly 83M. The Kickstarter amount is stated only as nearly double a 100,000 dollar goal so it is recorded as null. Vuzix, Epson and castAR sources are dated October 2013, two months after the August 2013 batch demo date. Disposition is a lender foreclosure and IP sale, not a clean acquisition, so exit is shutdown with the buyer in the reason. Company website metavision.com was not fetched.
